code: library(dtwSat)  samples <- st_read(system.file("mato_grosso_brazil/samples.gpkg", package = "dtwSat"), quiet = TRUE)  tif_files <- dir(system.file("mato_grosso_brazil", package = "dtwSat"), pattern = "\\.tif$", full.names = TRUE) tif_names <- basename(tif_files) acquisition_date <- as.Date(regmatches(tif_names, regexpr("[0-9]{8}", tif_names)), format = "%Y%m%d")  dc <- read_stars(tif_files,                  along = list(time = acquisition_date),                  RasterIO = list(bands = 1:6)) dc <- st_set_dimensions(dc, 3, c("EVI", "NDVI", "RED", "BLUE", "NIR", "MIR")) dc <- split(dc, c("band")) bands <- names(dc) labels <- samples$label  sample_cube <- st_extract(dc, samples) sample_ts <- sapply(bands, function(band) matrix(sample_cube[[band]], ncol = length(acquisition_date)), simplify = "array") pixel_ts <- sapply(bands, function(band) matrix(dc[[band]], ncol = length(acquisition_date)), simplify = "array")  dim(sample_ts) ## [1] 291  23   6 dim(pixel_ts) ## [1] 999  23   6

title: 2. Accuracy and processing time of TWDTW, DTW, random forest, and SVM
text: compare five models: TWDTW, GAM patterns: one temporal pattern land-use class, created Generalized Additive Model (GAM), first vignette. TWDTW, samples: time series training samples kept temporal patterns. DTW, GAM patterns: Dynamic Time Warping without time weight, calculated package dtw GAM patterns. matches time series pattern first last observation. Random forest: package randomForest, values bands dates predictors. SVM: package e1071, predictors. TWDTW arguments first vignette, packages default settings. model function trains samples id, classify() returns labels model gives array time series.
code: gam_fun <- function(data) mgcv::gam(y ~ s(x), data = data)  train_twdtw <- function(id, resampling_fun = NULL) {   twdtw_knn(x = sample_ts[id, , ],             y = labels[id],             time = acquisition_date,             resampling_fun = resampling_fun,             cycle_length = 'year',             time_scale = 'day',             time_weight = c(steepness = 0.1, midpoint = 50)) }  # The GAM patterns as matrices for the package dtw train_dtw <- function(id) {   model <- train_twdtw(id, gam_fun)   structure(list(labels = model$data$label,                  patterns = lapply(model$data$observations, function(pattern) as.matrix(pattern[bands]))),             class = "dtw_patterns") }  # One row for each time series, with the values of all bands on all dates predictors <- function(ts) matrix(ts, nrow = dim(ts)[1])  train <- list(   "TWDTW, GAM patterns" = function(id) train_twdtw(id, gam_fun),   "TWDTW, all samples"  = function(id) train_twdtw(id),   "DTW, GAM patterns"   = train_dtw,   "Random forest"       = function(id) randomForest::randomForest(predictors(sample_ts[id, , ]), factor(labels[id])),   "SVM"                 = function(id) e1071::svm(predictors(sample_ts[id, , ]), factor(labels[id])))  classify <- function(model, ts) {   if (inherits(model, "twdtw_knn")) {     predict(model, newdata = ts, time = acquisition_date)$prediction   } else if (inherits(model, "dtw_patterns")) {     # The label of the nearest pattern: dtw() is called for each time series and pattern     nearest <- apply(ts, 1, function(x) {       which.min(sapply(model$patterns, function(pattern) dtw::dtw(x, pattern, distance.only = TRUE)$distance))     })     model$labels[nearest]   } else {     predict(model, predictors(ts))   } }

code: set.seed(1)  group <- integer(nrow(samples)) for (label in unique(labels)) {   id <- which(labels == label)   group[id] <- kmeans(st_coordinates(samples)[id, ], centers = 5, nstart = 20)$cluster }  accuracy <- sapply(train, function(train_model) {   sapply(1:5, function(k) {     model <- train_model(which(group != k))     test <- which(group == k)     mean(classify(model, sample_ts[test, , ]) == labels[test])   }) }) accuracy_table <- data.frame(Mean = colMeans(accuracy),                              Lowest = apply(accuracy, 2, min),                              Highest = apply(accuracy, 2, max))  knitr::kable(100 * accuracy_table, digits = 1)

title: Time-Weighted Dynamic Time Warping for Satellite Image Time Series Analysis
text: Provides fast robust approach land use mapping using multi-dimensional (multi-band) satellite image time series. leveraging Time-Weighted Dynamic Time Warping (TWDTW) distance metric tandem k-nearest neighbour (KNN) classifier, package offers functions produce land use maps based distinct seasonality patterns, commonly observed phenological cycles vegetation. approach described Maus et al. (2016) Maus et al. (2019). primary advantage TWDTW capability handle irregularly sampled noisy time series, also requiring minimal training sets. package includes tools training KNN-TWDTW model, visualizing temporal patterns, producing land use maps, visualizing results. one temporal pattern land use class, classification data cube processing time comparable machine learning models available ‘R’, random forest support vector machines.

code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{  # Read training samples samples_path <-   system.file("mato_grosso_brazil/samples.gpkg", package = "dtwSat")  samples <- st_read(samples_path, quiet = TRUE)  # Get satellite image time series files tif_path <- system.file("mato_grosso_brazil", package = "dtwSat") tif_files <- dir(tif_path, pattern = "\\.tif$", full.names = TRUE)  # Get acquisition dates from the file names tif_names <- basename(tif_files) acquisition_date <- regmatches(tif_names, regexpr("[0-9]{8}", tif_names)) acquisition_date <- as.Date(acquisition_date, format = "%Y%m%d")  # Create a 3D datacube dc <- read_stars(tif_files,                  proxy = FALSE,                  along = list(time = acquisition_date),                  RasterIO = list(bands = 1:6)) dc <- st_set_dimensions(dc, 3, c("EVI", "NDVI", "RED", "BLUE", "NIR", "MIR")) dc <- split(dc, c("band"))  # Create a model with one temporal pattern for each label m <- twdtw_knn(  x = dc,  y = samples,  resampling_fun = function(data) mgcv::gam(y ~ s(x), data = data),  cycle_length = 'year',  time_scale = 'day',  time_weight = c(steepness = 0.1, midpoint = 50))  print(m)  # Visualize model patterns plot(m)  # Classify satellite images system.time(lu <- predict(m, newdata = dc))  # Visualise land use classification ggplot() +   geom_stars(data = lu["prediction"]) +   theme_minimal()  # Create a model with a custom resampling function: # the mean of the samples on each date m <- twdtw_knn(x = dc,  y = samples,  resampling_fun = function(data) lm(y ~ factor(x), data = data),  cycle_length = 'year',  time_scale = 'day',  time_weight = c(steepness = 0.1, midpoint = 50))  plot(m)  # Create a model that keeps the time series of all samples # and classify with the three nearest samples m <- twdtw_knn(x = dc,  y = samples,  cycle_length = 'year',  time_scale = 'day',  time_weight = c(steepness = 0.1, midpoint = 50))  lu <- predict(m, newdata = dc, k = 3)  # The share of the votes of each label among the three nearest samples lu_share <- predict(m, newdata = dc, k = 3, type = "prob")  # A data cube that does not fit in memory: a stars proxy object, which reads the # images when their values are needed. The files have seven bands. The first six # are selected after split(), and not with the argument RasterIO dc_proxy <- read_stars(tif_files, proxy = TRUE, along = "time") dc_proxy <- st_set_dimensions(dc_proxy, "time", values = acquisition_date) dc_proxy <- st_set_dimensions(dc_proxy, "band",                               values = c("EVI", "NDVI", "RED", "BLUE", "NIR", "MIR", "B7")) dc_proxy <- split(dc_proxy, c("band"))[1:6]  # The model reads the rows of the images that have samples m <- twdtw_knn(x = dc_proxy,  y = samples,  resampling_fun = function(data) mgcv::gam(y ~ s(x), data = data),  cycle_length = 'year',  time_scale = 'day',  time_weight = c(steepness = 0.1, midpoint = 50))  # The images are read and classified in blocks of 10 rows lu <- predict(m, newdata = dc_proxy, chunk_size = 10)  } # }
